faq_heading: Mountain View Homes for Sale in Chilliwack: your questions answered

faq.q: What do houses in Eastern Hillsides sell for?
faq.a: 56 houses sold in Eastern Hillsides from November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, at a median $1,142,500 after 24 days and 97.5% of the last list price. That covers every house in the area, not only those with a view.

faq.q: Which Chilliwack areas have mountain views?
faq.a: The hillside sub-areas, such as Eastern Hillsides, Promontory, Chilliwack Mountain and Little Mountain, are the likeliest. The search above shows listings currently flagged with a mountain view.

faq.q: How reliable is the view field on a listing?
faq.a: It is the listing agent's description, so confirm the view in person, in more than one kind of weather.

blocks.text: This search shows Chilliwack homes whose MLS® view field says Mountain View, live from the MLS®, with land and income properties left out. Chilliwack is built on flat farmland with mountains on three sides, and the hillside neighbourhoods are where the outlook is widest.
The hillsides and valleys around Chilliwack

Chilliwack's flat valley floor is ringed by mountains, and homes on the rising ground at the edge of town are the ones that look across it. In board terms those are sub-areas such as Eastern Hillsides, Promontory, Chilliwack Mountain and Little Mountain.

items.t: Yarrow sits between Vedder Mountain to the south and Sumas Mountain to the northwest, at the foot of the Skagit Range (Wikipedia, Neighbourhoods in Chilliwack).
Greendale lies at the base of Sumas Mountain, on the bed of the drained Sumas Lake.
Ryder Lake is a small sub-alpine farming community on Mount Thom.
The Chilliwack River Valley runs 47 km and is known for hiking and outdoor recreation.

blocks.text: The MLS® data has no view field, so a hillside sub-area median is a baseline for that sub-area. A view home on the same hill is likely priced above it, and how far above is best checked against recent sales on its own street.
What to check on a Chilliwack hillside view
Hillsides bring their own checks. The first two matter on almost every listing.

items.t: Ask about slope stability, drainage and retaining walls on any sloped lot, and read the geotechnical report if there is one.
Look at what could be built in front of the home under its zoning, and whether any of it is in the Agricultural Land Reserve.
On upland and rural lots, ask about water and septic, winter road access and snow clearing.
Visit on a clear morning and in rain. Mountain views on this side of the valley change a great deal with the weather.
